name: FLARE (Forward-Looking Active REtrieval)
executive_summary: Retrieves during generation when the model predicts low-confidence upcoming tokens. Adaptive retrieval that triggers only when needed, reducing unnecessary retrieval overhead.
description: FLARE monitors the model's confidence during generation. If confidence drops below a threshold, the current sentence is used as a query to retrieve additional context, and generation continues with augmented information.
when_to_use: Long-form generation where not all content requires external knowledge.
When up-front retrieval retrieves too much irrelevant context.
Streaming generation scenarios where retrieval can be interleaved.
when_not_to_use: Short-answer tasks where a single retrieval is sufficient.
When retrieval latency is too high for interleaved generation.
Models without confidence probability access (black-box APIs may not expose token probs).
known_pitfalls: Threshold tuning is critical; too low misses retrieval needs, too high wastes calls.
Retrieval latency can stall generation pipeline.
May retrieve redundant information if the model oscillates around the threshold.

primary_source.authors: Jiang, Xu, Gao, Sun, Liu, Dwivedi-Yu, Yang, Callan, Neubig
primary_source.title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation

usage_templates.template: Generate next sentence. If any token probability < {{threshold}}, treat the sentence as a query, retrieve relevant context, regenerate the sentence with retrieved context appended. Otherwise continue generation.

variables.name: threshold
variables.description: Confidence probability cutoff below which retrieval is triggered.

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: Adaptive number of retrieval calls depending on generation confidence. Requires access to token probabilities or explicit confidence estimation.
